note: What each Routes 1-3 water-event prop must still read of the water beside it. A water event's prop means something only in relation to its water: a jetty rack stands over the flats, a depth staff stands on a named shelf, an approach stops short of the shore. A reshaped heightmap can leave a prop's coordinates valid and its meaning wrong -- the 2026-09-28 water shape raised Viltri's bed under route2_viltri_sounding's deep staff by one block, so it read the same depth as the middle staff and the three shelves stopped reading differently. depth = level - rounded ground at the prop's own column (0 or less on dry land); waterline_distance = blocks to the nearest column the water covers, 0 when the prop's own column is wet. Both come from tools/ground.py, the canonical heightmap, never from a world. tools/route_events.py water_prop_problems() enforces this on every build; column is recorded so a drift report can name where the prop was sited.
bodies_note: Water is where the rounded ground is below the level, as WorldPainter paints it. The levels are the ones tools/route_events.py builds against (SEA_Y, VIltri_Y, POND_Y) and data/rivers.json lakes records.
tolerance_note: Deliberately tight. A single block of bed movement under a water prop is the failure this check exists to catch, and the answer is to re-site the prop and re-measure here, never to widen the tolerance.

the deep-mud approach on the south side, on dry shore a few blocks short of the pond edge
